|work=IBNLive}} As of January 2025, his net worth was estimated at US$5.0 billion, according to ''[[Forbes]]''.{{cite news |title=Forbes profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/nr-narayana-murthy/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017105115/https://www.forbes.com/profile/nr-narayana-murthy/ |archive-date=17 October 2020 |access-date=28 January 2025 |work=Forbes}} Murthy was born and raised in [[Sidlaghatta]], [[Karnataka]]. He first worked at the [[Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad]], as chief systems programmer, and [[Patni Computer Systems]] in [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]]. He founded Infosys in 1981 and was the CEO from 1981 to 2002, as well as the chairman from 2002 to 2011. In 2011, he stepped down from the board and became the chairman emeritus. In June 2013, Murthy was appointed as the executive chairman for a period of five years.{{cite news |date=1 June 2013 |title=Infosys appoints Narayana Murthy as Executive Chairman of the board, KV Kamath steps down |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/ites/infosys-appoints-narayana-murthy-as-executive-chairman-of-the-board-kv-kamath-steps-down/articleshow/20378690.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820074044/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/ites/infosys-appoints-narayana-murthy-as-executive-chairman-of-the-board-kv-kamath-steps-down/articleshow/20378690.cms |archive-date=20 August 2020 |access-date=1 June 2013 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}}{{cite news |title=Narayana Murthy Appointed as Additional Director and Executive Chairman of Infosys Board |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728060426/http://www.btvin.com/videos/watch/321/narayana-murthy-returns-to-revive-infosys |archive-date=28 July 2014 |publisher=[[Bloomberg TV India]]}} Murthy has been listed among the 12 greatest entrepreneurs of our time by ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' magazine.{{cite news |date=28 March 2012 |title=Narayana Murthy is among Fortune's 12 'greatest entrepreneurs' |url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/CorporateNews/Narayana-Murthy-is-among-Fortune-s-12-greatest-entrepreneurs/Article1-832212.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615003345/http://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/CorporateNews/Narayana-Murthy-is-among-Fortune-s-12-greatest-entrepreneurs/Article1-832212.aspx |archive-date=15 June 2012 |access-date=1 June 2013 |publisher=[[Hindustan Times]] |df=dmy-all}} He has been described as the "father of the Indian IT sector" by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine and [[CNBC]] for his contribution to outsourcing in India.{{cite news |date=15 August 2007 |title=INDIA'S INFLUENTIALS N.R. Narayana Murthy |url=http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1652689_1652372_1652367,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080506084241/http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1652689_1652372_1652367,00.html |archive-date=6 May 2008 |access-date=1 June 2013 |publisher=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}}{{cite news |title=CNBC 25: 13. Narayana Murthy |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2014/04/29/25-nr-narayana-murthy.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221026050717/https://www.cnbc.com/2014/04/29/25-nr-narayana-murthy.html |archive-date=26 October 2022 |access-date=13 April 2021}} In 2005, he co-chaired the [[World Economic Forum]] in [[Davos]], Switzerland.{{cite web |date=31 January 2005 |title=How to build a great company |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/jan/31spec.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111119025000/http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/jan/31spec.htm |archive-date=19 November 2011 |access-date=8 November 2011 |work=Rediff.com}} Murthy has been honoured with the [[Padma Vibhushan]]{{cite news |date=26 January 2008 |title=LN Mittal, Ratan Tata, Narayana Murthy get Padma Vibhushan |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2008-01-26/news/27713021_1_padma-vibhushan-padma-awards-second-highest-civilian-award |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130528081221/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2008-01-26/news/27713021_1_padma-vibhushan-padma-awards-second-highest-civilian-award |archive-date=28 May 2013 |access-date=2 June 2013 |publisher=Economic Times}} and [[Padma Shri]] awards. Murthy is the father-in-law of [[Rishi Sunak]], who was [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] from 2022 to 2024. ==Early life and education== N. R. Narayana Murthy was born on 20 August 1946 in [[Sidlaghatta]], a city in India's south-western state of [[Karnataka]]{{cite news |last=Subramanya |first=K.V. |date=9 March 2011 |title=He studied in Kannada medium till Class 10 |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/he-studied-in-kannada-medium-till-class-10/article1521724.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019085814/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/he-studied-in-kannada-medium-till-class-10/article1521724.ece |archive-date=19 October 2015 |access-date=27 April 2014 |work=The Hindu |location=Chennai, India}} into a Kannada speaking middle-class [[Deshastha Madhva Brahmin]] family.{{Cite web |date=26 July 2017 |title=A woman's place is in the kitchen: My experience as the only girl in engineering school in 1968 |url=https://qz.com/india/1038178/sudha-murthy-wife-of-infosys-founder-nr-narayana-murthy-recalls-being-only-girl-in-her-engineering-college/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806020519/https://qz.com/india/1038178/sudha-murthy-wife-of-infosys-founder-nr-narayana-murthy-recalls-being-only-girl-in-her-engineering-college/ |archive-date=6 August 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020}} After completing his school education, he went to the [[National Institute of Engineering]] and graduated in 1967 with a bachelor's degree in [[electrical engineering]]. In 1969 he received his master's degree from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]].{{cite news |title=Narayana Murthy's Childhood |url=http://teck.in/narayana-murthys-childhood.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019220116/https://teck.in/narayana-murthys-childhood.html |archive-date=19 October 2020 |access-date=1 June 2013}}{{cite news |title=Narayana Murthy on Achievers' Club |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6zJNc5KvWg0 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130129024048/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6zJNc5KvWg0&gl=US&hl=en |archive-date=2013-01-29 |access-date=1 June 2013}} In 2007, Murthy received an [[honorary degree]] from [[Lancaster University]].{{cite web |title=Honorary Graduates |url=https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/about-us/our-people/honorary-degrees/#2000s-431177-15 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240301095905/https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/about-us/our-people/honorary-degrees/#2000s-431177-15 |archive-date=1 March 2024 |access-date=1 March 2024 |website=Honorary Graduates}} ==Career== Murthy first worked as a [[research associate]] under a faculty at [[IIM Ahmedabad]] and then later as the chief systems programmer.{{cite web |title=485 Interview with N.R. Narayana Murthy |url=http://www.india-seminar.com/2000/485/485%20interview.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817062015/http://www.india-seminar.com/2000/485/485%20interview.htm |archive-date=17 August 2014 |access-date=7 March 2013 |publisher=India-seminar.com}} There he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed and implemented a BASIC interpreter for [[Electronics Corporation of India Limited]].{{cite web |title=Business Leaders NARAYANA MURTHY |url=http://www.in.com/narayana-murthy/biography-424.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501110713/http://www.in.com/narayana-murthy/biography-424.html |archive-date=1 May 2013 |access-date=2 June 2013}} He started a company named Softronics. When that company failed after about a year and a half, he joined [[Patni Computer Systems]] in [[Pune]].{{cite web |last=Roy |first=Prannoy |date=29 March 2008 |title=An Interview With Narayana Murthy |url=http://www.maheshonline.com/an-interview-with-narayana-murthy/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111228140208/http://www.maheshonline.com/an-interview-with-narayana-murthy/ |archive-date=28 December 2011 |access-date=7 March 2013 |work=maheshone}} Murthy mentions that being arrested and expelled for no good reason during the communist era 1974 in a border town near the [[SFR Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]]-[[Bulgaria]]n border, turned him into a "[[Humanistic capitalism|compassionate capitalist]]" from a "confused [[Left-wing politics|leftist]]/[[Communism in India|communist]]". In 1981 he, with six software professionals, founded [[Infosys]]{{cite web |date=6 January 2020 |title=NR Narayana Murthy's life changing incident |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/infosys-co-founder-narayana-murthy-recalls-incident-that-made-him-a-compassionate-capitalist/story/393212.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116073608/https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/infosys-co-founder-narayana-murthy-recalls-incident-that-made-him-a-compassionate-capitalist/story/393212.html |archive-date=16 January 2020 |access-date=27 March 2020 |publisher=businesstoday.in}}in Pune, {{cite news |title=NR Narayana Murthy's Profile, Founders of Infosys Technologies |url=http://studyrays.com/info/alltimegreat/business/nr-narayana-murthy.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130630091509/http://studyrays.com/info/alltimegreat/business/nr-narayana-murthy.php |archive-date=30 June 2013 |access-date=1 June 2013}}{{cite web |date=30 April 2011 |title=Infosys Announces Leadership Succession |url=http://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/pages/infosys-announces-leadership-succession.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531163923/http://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/pages/infosys-announces-leadership-succession.aspx |archive-date=31 May 2014 |access-date=7 March 2013 |work=Infosys}} with an initial capital investment of Rs 10,000, which was provided by his wife [[Sudha Murty]].{{cite web |date=20 August 2011 |title=Infosys Chairman Narayana Murthy Steps Down |url=http://www.yentha.com/news/view/1/13720 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130209210438/http://www.yentha.com/news/view/1/13720 |archive-date=9 February 2013 |access-date=20 August 2011 |work=yentha.com}} Murthy was the CEO of Infosys for 21 years from 1981 to 2002 and was succeeded by co-founder [[Nandan Nilekani]]. At Infosys he articulated, designed and implemented a global delivery model for IT services outsourcing from India.{{cite web |title=Management Profiles, N. R. Narayana Murthy |url=http://www.infosys.com/about/management-profiles/Pages/narayana-murthy.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531174740/http://www.infosys.com/about/management-profiles/pages/narayana-murthy.aspx |archive-date=31 May 2014 |access-date=1 June 2013 |publisher=Infosys Limited}} He was the chairman of the board from 2002 to 2006, after which he also became the chief mentor.[https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna14411071 Non-Executive Chairman – MSN Report] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224203948/https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna14411071 |date=24 February 2024 }}. In August 2011, he retired from the company, taking the title chairman emeritus. [[File:The Founder, Infosys, Shri N.R. Narayana Murthy calling on the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, in New Delhi on December 05, 2014.jpg|thumb|right|Murthy with [[Narendra Modi]] in 2014]] Murthy is an independent director on the corporate board of [[HSBC]] and has been a director on the boards of [[DBS Bank]], [[Unilever]], [[ICICI]] and [[NDTV]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20130602162359/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=398008&ticker=398006 Bloomberg Businessweek profile – N. R. Narayana Murthy CBE] He is also a member of the advisory boards and councils of several educational and philanthropic institutions, including [[Cornell University]], [[INSEAD]], [[ESSEC]], [[Ford Foundation]], the [[UN Foundation]], the Indo-British Partnership, Asian Institute of Management, a trustee of the [[Infosys Prize]], a trustee of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, and as a trustee of the Rhodes Trust.{{cite web |title=The Rhodes Trust and Trustees – The Rhodes Trust |url=http://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/page/trustees |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807173028/http://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/page/trustees |archive-date=7 August 2011 |access-date=8 November 2011 |publisher=Rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk}} He is also the Chairman of the Governing board of [[Public Health Foundation of India]].{{cite news |date=12 July 2011 |title=Narayana Murthyto chair PHFI |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/article2219732.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026030302/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/article2219732.ece |archive-date=26 October 2012 |access-date=19 July 2011 |newspaper=The Hindu |location=Chennai, India}} He is on the Asia Pacific advisory board of [[BT Group plc|British Telecommunications]].{{cite web |date=20 August 1946 |title=United Nations Foundation – N. R. Narayana Murthy (India) |url=http://www.unfoundation.org/who-we-are/board/n-r-narayana-murthy.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308113141/http://www.unfoundation.org/who-we-are/board/n-r-narayana-murthy.html |archive-date=8 March 2012 |access-date=8 November 2011 |publisher=Unfoundation.org}} In June 2013, Murthy returned to Infosys as executive chairman and a director.{{Cite web |title=Infosys Board appoints Mr. N R Narayana Murthy as Executive Chairman of the Board |url=https://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/2013/nrn-executive-chairman.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305175602/https://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/2013/nrn-executive-chairman.html |archive-date=5 March 2024 |access-date=2024-02-01 |website=www.infosys.com}} In June 2014, he stood down as executive chairman, was non-executive chairman until October, when he became chairman emeritus.{{cite web |date=12 June 2014 |title=Vishal Sikka to be CEO and MD of Infosys, Murthy Non-Executive Chairman |url=http://news.biharprabha.com/2014/06/vishal-sikka-to-be-ceo-and-md-of-infosys-from-august-1/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715065419/http://news.biharprabha.com/2014/06/vishal-sikka-to-be-ceo-and-md-of-infosys-from-august-1/ |archive-date=15 July 2014 |access-date=12 June 2014 |publisher=news.biharprabha.com}} Murthy is also on the strategic board which advises the national law firm, [[Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas]], on strategic, policy and governance issues.{{cite news |last1=Vyas |first1=Maulik |title=Cyril Shroff ropes in business luminaries like Narayana Murthy, Deepak Parekh, Uday Kotak and others for advisory board of his law firm |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/consultancy-/-audit/cyril-shroff-ropes-in-business-luminaries-like-narayana-murthy-deepak-parekh-uday-kotak-and-others-for-advisory-board-of-his-law-firm/articleshow/48417617.cms |access-date=10 August 2015 |work=The Economic Times}} He is a member of [[IESE Business School|IESE's]] International Advisory Board (IAB).[https://www.iese.edu/about/leadership/ ''Members of IESE's International Advisory Board''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301070750/https://www.iese.edu/about/leadership/ |date=1 March 2019 }}, iese.edu In 2010, Murthy has made an investment in SKS Microfinance along with venture capitalist Vinod Khosla. {{Cite web |date=2010-04-09 |title=Profiting from poverty? SKS Microfinance IPO sparks debate: Narayana Murthy |url=https://www.livemint.com/Money/PEPcriJKTDeSRgsuprwL8O/Profiting-from-poverty-SKS-Microfinance-IPO-sparks-debate.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231153236/https://www.livemint.com/Money/PEPcriJKTDeSRgsuprwL8O/Profiting-from-poverty-SKS-Microfinance-IPO-sparks-debate.html |archive-date=31 December 2025 |access-date=2010-04-09 |website=livemint |language=en}} In 2016, Murthy participated in FXC as a Board Member. In 2017, Murthy raised concerns over alleged corporate governance lapses at Infosys, however the company went on to deny these claims.{{Cite web |last=Sood |first=Anirban Sen, Varun |date=2017-08-18 |title=Narayana Murthy raises issues at Infosys again |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/eeK2B7ISo6JWXZlSBnecMO/Infosys-directors-said-Sikka-not-CEO-material-Narayana-Murth.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200313195003/https://www.livemint.com/Companies/eeK2B7ISo6JWXZlSBnecMO/Infosys-directors-said-Sikka-not-CEO-material-Narayana-Murth.html |archive-date=13 March 2020 |access-date=2020-04-09 |website=Livemint |language=en}} == Views on working hours == In late 2023, a comment by Murthy suggesting that young people should work 70 hours a week to boost Nagavara Ramarao Narayana Murthy (born 20 August 1946) is an Indian billionaire businessman. He is the founder of Infosys, and was the chairman, chief executive officer (CEO), president and chief mentor of the company before retiring and becoming chairman emeritus. As of January 2025, his net worth was estimated at US$5.0 billion, according to Forbes.
Murthy was born and raised in Sidlaghatta, Karnataka. He first worked at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, as chief systems programmer, and Patni Computer Systems in Pune, Maharashtra. He founded Infosys in 1981 and was the CEO from 1981 to 2002, as well as the chairman from 2002 to 2011. In 2011, he stepped down from the board and became the chairman emeritus. In June 2013, Murthy was appointed as the executive chairman for a period of five years.
Murthy has been listed among the 12 greatest entrepreneurs of our time by Fortune magazine. He has been described as the "father of the Indian IT sector" by Time magazine and CNBC for his contribution to outsourcing in India. In 2005, he co-chaired the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland. Murthy has been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and Padma Shri awards.
Murthy is the father-in-law of Rishi Sunak, who was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2022 to 2024.
